seed.relationship: a landlord's son and a tenant's daughter
seed.conflict: over an unfair rule everyone obeys
seed.topicSeed: a fishing harbor in Hanoi; a landlord's son and a tenant's daughter over an unfair rule everyone obeys

g.passage:
When the boats come in at dawn to the harbor in Hanoi,
the rule is old: the tenants' catch is weighed first,
and the landlord's scale is always kind to the landlord.
Everyone obeys. My father obeys. I, Aoife, obey,
my hands smelling of salt and silence.
But this morning Somchai, the landlord's son,
stood at the scale and read the true weight aloud,
loud enough for the gulls, loud enough for the nets.
My heart knocked like a hull against the pier,
afraid of what his father would say,
and still I lifted my basket higher
so the whole dock could see the numbers.
Somewhere a bell rang for the market.
A woman sold green mangoes from a bicycle,
and the river kept pushing its brown water toward the sea.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the poem?
options: Fearful and anxious, with only a faint glimmer of courage
Resigned, accepting an unfair rule as something unchangeable
Defiantly hopeful, though shadowed by some lingering fear
Nostalgic, fondly recalling the familiar routines of harbor life
g.explanation: 시는 모두가 불공정한 규칙에 복종한다는 체념으로 시작하지만, Somchai가 진짜 무게를 크게 읽고 화자가 바구니를 더 높이 드는 장면에서 반항적 희망이 두드러진다. 심장이 선체처럼 부두에 부딪힌다는 표현은 두려움을 함께 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, B는 앞부분의 체념만 말하며, D의 향수는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

seed.conflict: after discovering a letter meant for someone else

seed.topicSeed: a rooftop water tank in Kingston; a conductor and the youngest violinist after discovering a letter meant for someone else

g.passage: Years ago, when the orchestra rehearsed in a Kingston warehouse, Younghee, its youngest violinist, practiced alone beside the rooftop water tank, where the heat bent the air and no one could hear her mistakes. One afternoon she found a folded letter tucked beneath the tank's iron ladder. It praised “the girl who plays the hard passage twelve times without complaint,” and it was signed with an L, the initial of Linton, the conductor. She blushed so fiercely that she nearly dropped her bow. Only later did she learn it was a draft recommendation for another student, a cellist who also practiced up there. Even so, she carried the phrase with her for years, playing the hard passage twelve times, then thirteen. Below, the street vendors called out the price of ackee and saltfish.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Chiefly mortified, with just a trace of lingering fondness
Bitter, resenting the praise given to a different student
Embarrassed, focused mainly on a mistaken reading of a letter
Tenderly reflective, with a flash of youthful embarrassment
g.explanation: Younghee가 편지를 자기 이야기로 오해해 얼굴을 붉히는 장면에는 당혹감이 있지만 짧게 지나간다. 그 뒤로도 그 문구를 오래 간직하며 어려운 구절을 열세 번까지 연습했다는 회상이 애틋하고 사려 깊은 분위기를 주도하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, B의 원망은 단서가 약하며, C는 덜 두드러진 당혹감만 말한다.

seed.relationship: a pair of lifelong friends who rarely speak
seed.conflict: about teaching a skill that is dying out
seed.topicSeed: an old cinema projection booth in Kerala; a pair of lifelong friends who rarely speak about teaching a skill that is dying out

g.passage: Warm celluloid and machine oil: that smell still returns to me whenever it rains. In the projection booth of the old cinema in Kerala, Rajendra taught Zeynep to splice film without saying more than a dozen words a night. They had been friends since childhood, and talk had long ago become unnecessary between them. He would hold a strip up to the bulb, and she would nod; he would press the cement, and she would count the seconds under her breath. Everyone in town said that soon no theater would need such hands, and some nights the empty seats below seemed to agree. Yet the two of them worked as though each careful join were a promise. Rain drummed on the corrugated roof, and a bat slipped out through the vent.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Quietly devoted, shaded by a sense of loss
Mournful, with only a passing hint of devotion
Regretful, focused on the decline of the cinema
Playful, celebrating a friendship built on teasing
g.explanation: 두 친구는 말없이도 서로 호흡을 맞추며 이음 하나하나를 약속처럼 다루어 조용한 헌신이 지문의 중심을 이룬다. 곧 이런 손이 필요 없어질 것이라는 마을 사람들의 말과 빈 객석은 사라지는 기술에 대한 상실감을 더하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, C는 덜 두드러진 쇠퇴만 말하며, D의 장난스러움은 지문에 단서가 약하다.

seed.relationship: a nurse and her night patient
seed.conflict: over how to describe an accident honestly
seed.topicSeed: a rooftop laundry line in Busan; a nurse and her night patient over how to describe an accident honestly

g.passage: How do you tell a man the truth about his own fall? That was the question I carried up to the hospital roof in Busan each night, where I hung the ward's towels on the laundry line after my shift. Chulsoo, my night patient, had slipped from scaffolding, and his foreman, Gyeongho, wanted the report to say he had been careless. Chulsoo insisted the harness had been frayed. One night he asked me to write down his account exactly, and when I hesitated, he said, “You are the only one here who does not finish my sentences.” I wrote every word, then read it back to him twice. Afterward he asked, half joking, whether I would visit the scaffolding with him once he could walk. The towels snapped in the wind, and below us the harbor cranes swung their red lights over the water.
g.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between the narrator and Chulsoo?
options: A patient who distrusts his nurse and suspects that she sides with his foreman
A nurse who depends on her patient to help her finish her nightly chores
A typical hospital arrangement in which the nurse keeps a cool distance
A nurse and patient bound by trust built on her careful attention to his words
g.explanation: Chulsoo는 화자에게만 자신의 진술을 그대로 받아 적어 달라고 부탁하며 그녀가 자기 말을 끊지 않는 유일한 사람이라고 말한다. 화자가 한 글자도 빼지 않고 적어 두 번 읽어 주고, 이후 Chulsoo가 반농담으로 함께 비계를 보러 가자고 하는 데서 신뢰가 확인되므로 D가 정답이다. A는 한쪽의 의심만 내세웠고, B는 의존의 방향이 반대이며, C는 일반적 통념에서 나온 관계다.
